title: Ferroelectric--Superconducting Interaction in Epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7-δ/BaTiO3 Films
authors: Louis Oppong-Antwi, David L. Cortie, Qi Zhang, Avi Bendavid, Nagarajan Valanoor, Wendy Purches, Golrokh Akhgar
abstract: Microscopic theories predict that the critical temperature of a superconducting layer can be strongly modified in proximity to a ferroelectric; however, experimental evidence is lacking. We report on BaTiO3 (BTO)/YBa2Cu3O7-δ (YBCO) heterostructures grown on SrTiO3 (001) substrates using pulsed laser deposition (PLD), with precise control of growth conditions and oxygen stoichiometry. Piezoresponse force microscopy confirms ferroelectric switching within both single-layer and heterostructured films. Neutron reflectometry measurements show low roughness parameters for the buried interfaces, which is critical for mediating the interfacial coupling between superconductivity and ferroelectric polarization. The superconducting transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{C}}^{R}$) measured from the $R(T)$ curve of the single-layer YBCO was approximately 86 K, and a transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{C}}^{M}$) of approximately 80-85 K was observed from the $M(T)$ curve. For the heterostructure film (YBCO/BTO/YBCO) grown under the same conditions, both resistivity and magnetization measurements indicate lower transition temperatures of approximately 75 K and approximately 55 K, respectively, as well as a lower overall susceptibility. These findings highlight the need to combine multiple techniques to characterize BTO/YBCO heterostructures and identify subtle features of the ferroelectric--superconducting coupling. This establishes BTO/YBCO heterostructures as promising systems for tunable oxide electronics and reconfigurable superconducting devices.
summary: The authors report on $	ext{BTO}/	ext{YBCO}$ heterostructures to experimentally investigate the predicted coupling between ferroelectric polarization and superconductivity. By measuring $T_c$ using resistivity and magnetization, they demonstrate that the inclusion of the BTO layer significantly lowers the superconducting transition temperature in YBCO films. This establishes these interfaces as promising platforms for engineering tunable quantum electronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates how ferroelectric polarization influences the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) in epitaxial oxide heterostructures.
main_result: The presence of a $	ext{BaTiO}_3$ layer significantly suppresses the superconducting transition temperatures measured via both resistivity and magnetization curves compared to single-layer YBCO films.
method: The research employed multiple advanced characterization techniques, including Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD) for film growth, Piezoresponse Force Microscopy (PFM), Neutron Reflectometry (NR), and transport/magnetization measurements ($R(T)$ and $M(T)$).
model_or_system: The physical system is epitaxial $	ext{BaTiO}_3/	ext{YBa}_2	ext{Cu}_3	ext{O}_{7-\delta}$ ($	ext{BTO}/	ext{YBCO}$) heterostructures grown on $	ext{SrTiO}_3$ substrates. The study focuses on the interfacial coupling between ferroelectric polarization and superconducting pairing.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperatures ($T_{\mathrm{C}}^{R}$, $T_{\mathrm{C}}^{M}$), ferroelectric switching behavior (PFM hysteresis loops), film roughness, and lattice parameters.
important_parameters: The coupling strength between polarization and superconductivity; the oxygen stoichiometry ($\delta$) in YBCO; and the thickness of the BTO layer relative to superconducting coherence lengths.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that the observed suppression of $T_c$ can be attributed to interfacial charge screening, strain effects, or structural disorder induced by the ferroelectric layer.
figures_summary: Figures likely show PFM hysteresis loops confirming switching, XRD patterns verifying epitaxial growth, and $R(T)$ vs. $M(T)$ curves demonstrating the suppression of $T_c$ in the heterostructure compared to single layers.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of establishing the physical platform ($	ext{BTO}/	ext{YBCO}$ films), characterizing both ferroelectric and superconducting properties using multiple techniques, presenting quantitative measurements showing $T_c$ suppression, and concluding with implications for tunable oxide electronics.
why_interesting: This work directly probes an interface where two distinct quantum phenomena—superconductivity (BCS-like pairing) and ferroelectricity (polar ordering)—interact, which is a key area of research in correlated electron systems and emergent quantum states.
